entries.name: 3x3min Pursuit Bridge (88-92% MAP)
entries.description:
Intent: Bridge the 2-min to 3-min VO2 durability gap. MAP = 394w.

Warm-up: 15 min progressive Z1-Z3 with 2 x 30s VO2 openers.
Main set: 3 x 3 min @ 88-92% MAP (347-362w). Cap 95% (374w).
First 30s of each rep at 95% MAP to simulate pursuit start, then settle to 88-92% MAP.
Recovery: 5 min easy between reps.
Cool-down: 10 min easy.

Success criteria: Hold 88-92% MAP through the final 60 sec of each rep without power decay. These are CONTROLLED efforts — not max.

entries.name: Track — pursuit pacing, flying runs (no-fade focus)
entries.description:
- Warm-up — build to race cadence, then two or three short openers, then full recovery. CORRECTION (30 Jul): power IS recorded — SRM on the track bike. Judge every run on lap splits first, power second. The original note here said there was no power on the fixed gear; that was wrong. 20m 210w

- Run one — flying six laps at your race-schedule lap pace. EVEN splits, rehearse the schedule. 1m40s 390w

- Full recovery — easy roll or spin 10m 120w

- Run two — flying six laps, NEGATIVE split: ease the first two laps, build the last two. 1m40s 390w

- Full recovery — easy roll or spin 10m 120w

- Run three — flying eight laps (full pursuit distance) at controlled sub-race pace, hold the split. PROTECT this rep if legs or time run short — it is the over-distance durability rep. 2m15s 370w

- Full recovery — easy roll or spin 10m 120w

- Run four — OPTIONAL if the legs feel good: flying six laps, honest even pace, zero fade on the last two laps (mini-test). 1m40s 390w

- Cooldown — easy spin. Strength number two follows in the PM, a few hours later. OUTCOME (analysed 30 Jul): run one ridden even as prescribed (16.36, 16.23, 16.11, 16.10, 16.09, 16.24); run two negative-split as instructed (16.63 down to 15.81); run three ridden at sub-race pace but built rather than holding the split (16.96 down to 16.06). Session design gap: no standing start, which is where the tractable time actually sits. 10m 140w

steps.text: Warm-up — build to race cadence, then two or three short openers, then full recovery. CORRECTION (30 Jul): power IS recorded — SRM on the track bike. Judge every run on lap splits first, power second. The original note here said there was no power on the fixed gear; that was wrong.
Run one — flying six laps at your race-schedule lap pace. EVEN splits, rehearse the schedule.
Full recovery — easy roll or spin
Run two — flying six laps, NEGATIVE split: ease the first two laps, build the last two.

Run three — flying eight laps (full pursuit distance) at controlled sub-race pace, hold the split. PROTECT this rep if legs or time run short — it is the over-distance durability rep.

entries.name: Track — standing starts + flat pursuit distance (108 inch)
entries.description:
- Kit and gear: 64x16 (108 inch) on 165 mm cranks, TRAINING SUIT. The race suit is worth 0.33s per lap — save it for benchmarks so these splits stay comparable to 12 Jul. Warm up BEFORE you arrive; use the track allocation for rolling laps, three or four progressive half-lap accelerations, and one lap above target cadence. Nothing anaerobic. 20m 210w

- Gate one — standing start, one lap, full gas. THIS IS THE PRIORITY. Nationals standing lap was 23.21s and you were 0.33s down on 2025. Beat 23.21. Note the feel of the first three strokes. 108 inch gives about 1.5 percent less pedal force than the gear that produced it, but is still about 1.5 percent heavier than the 110 inch and 170 mm that produced the 2025 gate — a partial fix, not a full one. 30s 550w

- Full recovery — easy rolling laps 10m 120w

- Gate two — standing start, one lap, full gas. Two reps because one tells you nothing. 30s 550w

- Full recovery — easy rolling laps 13m 120w

- Main rep — standing start, full pursuit distance, eight laps. Hold laps two to eight FLAT at 16.35s, plus or minus 0.15. Cadence about 109 rpm. That is the Nationals flying-lap mean of 16.03s plus the training-suit offset, so holding it flat matches the title ride in a slower suit. Lap two must ALREADY be on target — opening slow and finishing fast is a failed rep whatever the total says. If protecting Sunday matters more, hold 16.60s instead: same shape, much cheaper. Judge on lap splits, not on the watts — the wattage here is only for load projection. 2m20s 380w

- Full recovery — easy rolling laps 13m 120w

- Optional gear comparison — only if the main rep held flat. Flying six laps, even, at 16.20s. Straight A-B against run one on 12 Jul, which averaged 16.19s on 110 inch. Compare cadence and RPE. Read it loosely: it is not fatigue-matched to 12 Jul. 1m40s 390w

- Cooldown — easy spin. Record power. The track SRM looks 8 to 12 percent low against measured CdA, so log the numbers for a KICKR cross-check. Pacing note: flattening the race profile is worth only about 0.15s aerodynamically — the main rep is a physiological experiment (does a calmer open preserve back-half power?), and the gate is where the real time is. 15m 140w

entries.name: Track — flying race-distance runs, hold the floor
entries.description:
- Before you leave: pump the rear tub hard, and roll the rear wheel out over five revolutions and write the number down — that settles whether the training rollout is race spec or oversize, and every training-to-race comparison depends on it. Kit: TRAINING SUIT. Warm up before you arrive; track time is for rolling laps and three or four progressive half-lap accelerations. Nothing anaerobic, no starts. 20m 210w

- Run one entry — two rolling laps building, so you cross the line already at target. Do not wind up inside the scored distance. 1m30s 260w

- Run one — flying seven laps. Hold 16.35 FLAT, plus or minus 0.10. That is the Nationals flying mean converted to the training suit, so holding it flat matches the title ride pace in a slower suit. First scored lap must ALREADY be on target. Judge on splits, not watts. 1m55s 400w

- Full recovery — easy rolling laps 14m 120w

- Run two entry — same wind-up, same line 1m30s 260w

- Run two — flying seven laps, 16.35 FLAT again. THIS IS THE SESSION. Run two must match run one within about a tenth on the mean. One run tells you the pace exists; two tells you it repeats, which is what a round-based championship actually asks for. If run one drifted, hold the same target here rather than chasing it back. 1m55s 400w

- Full recovery — easy rolling laps 14m 120w

- Run three entry 1m30s 260w

- Run three — flying four laps at 16.00. Shorter and faster, to touch race opening speed and read the top end without paying for another long rep. Skip this if run two was a struggle — runs one and two are the session, this is the bonus. 1m4s 425w

- Full recovery — easy rolling laps 8m 120w

- Optional, only if you get a fourth slot — steady four minutes at one constant, comfortable lap split, held dead level, and note the SRM average. Tomorrow ride the same wattage on the KICKR and compare heart rate and RPE. Closes the track power question that currently makes every percentage-of-MAP claim about track work approximate. 4m 300w

- Cooldown — easy spin, record power. 15m 140w
